summary: A Delivery at `review` or `awaiting_merge` whose Delivery Review record exists but cannot be read, for example after an editor wrote a byte order mark, no longer reads as a Delivery that recorded no PR. Only that record says whether the PR was recorded, so the Delivery compiler now reports its merge state as unknown with a finding that names the record, and `delivery_compile.py check` and `status` fail with it, as they fail when Git cannot decide the merge. So does a Delivery at `awaiting_merge` whose Review record is missing or has no `pull_request_url`: the commit that records the PR URL in the Review is the one that sets `awaiting_merge`, so that record is broken, not one that recorded no PR. A Delivery at `review` without a Review record, or whose Review has no `pull_request_url`, still recorded no PR yet, and a readable record that names its PR is derived as before. Every reader of that merge state takes the finding as unknown instead of guessing from the tracked status: `on --goal delivery:DLV-###` refuses the goal and a running grant shows it as unknown with the reason, the story size budget measures only the stories the backlog revision changes and names the finding in `skipped_stories`, and the pre-handoff selection at process switch `pre_handoff_regression` value `touched_suites` refuses through the same finding, which replaces its own check of that record.
